learning_outcomes.text: Apply Maxwell's equations and Gauss's and Stokes' theorems to solve simple electromagnetic situations.
Understand the behavior of material aggregates in electric and magnetic fields and comprehend the basis of different simplified models (conductors, dielectrics, magnets,…).
Link the purely formal and mathematical theory of electromagnetism with technical applications based on simplifications.
Experimentally measure charges, charge densities, electric and magnetic fields, etc.
Write reports on experimental practices carried out in the Advanced Electromagnetism laboratory, including error treatment.

syllabus_topics: Derivation and integration in scalar and vector fields.

First-order derivatives in scalar and vector fields: gradient, divergence and curl. Second-order derivatives: Laplacians. Integration in fields: scalar and vector potentials. Laplace-Poisson equations for potentials.
Stationary fields in the absence of material aggregates.

Heaviside-Lorentz force. Maxwell's equations for electric and magnetic fields. Stationary case. Deduction of Coulomb's and Biot-Savart's laws. Symmetric situations: application of Gauss' and Stokes' theorems. Electric and magnetic dipoles.
Stationary fields in the presence of material aggregates.

Macroscopic models of matter. Conductive and dielectric materials. Magnetic and non-magnetic materials. Hysteresis. Ohm's and Joule's laws for stationary current conduction. Electric and magnetic forces on matter. Equivalent polarization charges and equivalent magnetization currents. Electric displacement and magnetic magnetization fields. Electric and magnetic circuits. Maxwell's equations in the presence of material aggregates.

Uniqueness theorem for electrostatic situations. Method of resolution by electric images. Influence matrices: capacity coefficients and inductances. Field discontinuities. Numerical calculation methods.
Conditions defining quasistationary situations. Magnetic field in a capacitor and electric field in an inductor. Faraday-Henry induction law and conditions for its validity.
Time-varying fields in the absence of material aggregates.
Time-varying fields in free space: D'Alembert's equations. Electromagnetic waves in free space. General solution of D'Alembert's equations: retarded potentials.
Time-varying fields in the presence of material aggregates.

Time-varying fields in material aggregates. Electromagnetic waves in linear dielectric and conductive materials. Energy in electromagnetic fields and waves. Poynting's theorem. Reference systems for Maxwell's equations.

Attendance control and active participation in the course (continuous assessment)
Objective theoretical and/or practical individual tests (final assessment)

assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by summing the scores from all four sections, provided that a minimum of 1 point out of 4 is obtained in each of the objective tests (first and last sections), a minimum of 3.5 points out of 8 for both objective tests combined, and a minimum of 0.5 points out of 1 for laboratory practices. Failure to meet these minimums results in failing the course. On the day of the final exam, students can take a complementary exam to change their continuous assessment objective test score. This applies to ordinary (June) and extraordinary (July) calls. Students who do not attend the final exam will be marked as 'not presented'. Up to two justified absences from laboratory practices can be recovered, subject to resource availability.
